title: UPSC CSE - Indian Geography - Physiography of India
subject: Indian Geography

questions.q:
Consider the following information :
Waterfall Region River
1. Dhuandhar Malwa Narmada
2. Hundru Chota Nagpur Subarnarekha
3. Gersoppa Western Ghats Netravati
In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.explain: At the heart of India, dissected by mighty Narmada, are the marble cliffs of Bhedaghat and the roaring falls of Dhuandhar in the Jabalpur District of Madhya Pradesh. Malwa, a region in west-central northern India, occupies a plateau of volcanic origin in the western part of Madhya Pradesh state. The region includes the Madhya Pradesh districts of Dewas, Dhar, Indore, Jhabua, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Rajgarh, Ratlam, Shajapur, Ujjain, and parts of Guna and Sehore, and the Rajasthan districts of Jhalawar and parts of Banswara and Chittorgarh. It does not cover Jabalpur. Thus the Dhuandhar falls, though situated at the Narmada river, are not a part of the Malwa Plateau. Hence, pair 1 is not correctly matched. The Hundru Falls, Ranchi is created on the course of the Subarnarekha River, where it falls from a height of 320 feet creating the highest waterfalls of the state. It is situated at a distance of 45 kilometres from the main city of Ranchi. The Falls is a surprise package for the visitors who love the panoramic view of the Chota Nagpur Plateau. Hence, pair 2 is correctly matched. Gersoppa Falls (Jog Falls), a major attraction in Karnataka, is located in the Shimoga district of Karnataka. Also known by alternative names of Gerusoppe Falls and Jogada Gundi. Four cascades, known as Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket merge to form the huge waterfall on the Sharavathi River (and not Netravati River). Hence, pair 3 is not correctly matched. The Sharavathi River basin is situated in the central part of the Western Ghats. The river in the central Western Ghats is recognized as a hot speck in the biodiversity hotspot. Only one pair is correctly matched: Hundru-Chota Nagpur-Subernarekha

questions.q: Which one of the following is the best example of repeated falls in sea level, giving rise to present-day extensive marshland?
questions.explain: Coastal regions and certain inland areas are shaped by historical changes in sea levels. The Rann of Kutch is a prime example of land formed by repeated falls in sea level, leading to extensive marshlands and salt flats.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Namcha Barwa - Garhwal Himalaya
2. Nanda Devi - Kumaon Himalaya
3. Nokrek - Sikkim Himalaya
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Pair 1 is not correct: Namcha Barwa is in Arunachal Himalayas. Pair 2 is correct: Nanda Devi is in Kumaon Himalayas. Pair 3 is not correct: Nokrek is in Garo Hills, Meghalaya.
questions.subject: Indian Geography

questions.q: Siachen Glacier is situated in the:
questions.explain: The Siachen Glacier is in the Eastern Karakoram range in the Himalayas. It is situated to the North of Nubra Valley. It is the Second-Longest glacier in the World's Non-Polar areas.

questions.q:
Which of the following Protected Areas are located in the Cauvery basin?
1. Nagarhole National Park
2. Papikonda National Park
3. Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve
4. Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Nagarhole National Park, Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, and Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary are located in the Cauvery basin. Papikonda National Park is located in the Godavari basin.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India, the Himalayas are spread over five states only.
2. The Western Ghats are spread over five states only.
3. Pulicat Lake is spread over two States only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Indian Himalayan Region is spread across 12 Indian States. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Western Ghats traverse 6 states. Statement 3 is correct: Pulicat Lake is spread over Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
questions.subject: Indian Geography

questions.q: Which of the following is geographically closest to Great Nicobar?
questions.explain: The closest landmass to Great Nicobar in the south is Sumatra, which is located at a distance of 145 km.
questions.subject: Indian Geography

questions.q: From the ecological point of view, which one of the following assumes importance in being a good link between the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats?
questions.explain: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve is located in Kerala. It is located in the Eastern and Western Ghats, forming a good link between them.
questions.subject: Indian Geography

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of States of India indicates the easternmost and westernmost State?
questions.explain: Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat are the easternmost and westernmost States of India.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Hills - Region
1. Cardamom Hills - Coromandel Coast
2. Kaimur Hills - Konkan Coast
3. Mahadeo Hills - Central India
4. Mikir Hills - North-East India
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Cardamom Hills are in the Malabar Coast. Kaimur Hills are in the Vindhya Range. Mahadeo Hills are in central India. Mikir Hills are in North-East India.

questions.q:
The Narmada River flows to the west, while most other large peninsular rivers flow to the east. Why?
1. It occupies a linear rift valley.
2. It flows between the Vindhyas and the Satpuras.
3. The land slopes to the west from Central India.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: The Narmada flows towards the west in a rift valley formed due to faulting. It is bounded by the Vindhyas on the north and the Satpuras on the south.
